title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 47-50): Grothendieck is axiomatizing the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space. It is a contravariant system d ↦ Σ*(d), indexed by finite nonempty totally ordered sets d = {i_0<...<i_n}, which play the role of chains (flags) of strata. Σ*(0) is the unfolded stratum, a manifold with boundary. Σ*(1) maps to Σ*(0) by a 'source' map (proper and fibrant) and by a 'bord' map whose image is the boundary. Σ*(d) for longer chains are the iterated 'corner' pieces.

Previous page: condition (32) says the square attached to a pushout of ordered sets d'' = d ∪ d', δ = d ∩ d' is cocartesian. Diagram (33) maps Σ*(d) through Σ*({i_α, i_n}) to Σ*({i_n}), with 'bordant' maps φ_α (inclusions of boundary-type subspaces).

This page makes (33) precise as a local corner/transversality axiom. Near each point of Σ*(d), viewed inside Σ*({i_n}) ≅ Σ*(0):
- Σ*(d) should be the intersection of the n images of Σ*({i_α, i_n}), each ≅ Σ*(1) and each a boundary hypersurface ('partie bordante').
- This family of hypersurfaces should be transversal.
In modern terms: Σ*(d) is locally a codimension-n corner of a manifold with corners, cut out transversally by the boundary hypersurfaces labelled by the elements of d other than the last.

He then states the analogous condition for every morphism Σ*(d') → Σ*(d), with d ⊂ d' and d, d' 'cofinal' (same largest element). For this he uses the intermediate chains d ∪ {j}, j ∈ d' \ d. This gives diagram (34): a fan Σ*(d') → Σ*(d ∪ {j_1}), ..., Σ*(d ∪ {j_p}), each bordant into Σ*(d). This generalizes (33) and makes the transversality condition explicit: Σ*(d') should be the transversal intersection, inside Σ*(d), of the bordant subspaces Σ*(d ∪ {j}).

He concludes that, near the relevant points, all spaces are identified with subspaces of Σ*({a}) ≅ Σ*(0). Generically (cf. condition (b)) these subspaces are partial intersections of certain bordant subspaces of Σ*({a}) cutting each other transversally. Put simply, the unfolded system is locally modelled on the face lattice of a manifold with embedded corners: faces correspond to chains of strata, and inclusions of faces correspond to refinements of chains.

The problem served: a purely 'tame' / manifold-theoretic description of stratified spaces (via their conical neighbourhoods), equivalent to the stratified space itself, as announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the page is a draft of an axiom. One gap: the requirement that d, d' be cofinal (same last element) is needed because only maps preserving the last element are 'bordant'. Non-cofinal inclusions give 'source'-type fibrant maps (next page, condition (c)), and the page does not yet say how the two kinds of maps interact. The marginal note on the next page shows he is himself unsure whether the description of the boundary of Σ*(d') follows from condition (d) ('délicat', cf. Σ*({0,2})).

The claim 'cela implique la chose analogue pour tous morphismes Σ*(d') → Σ*(d)' is asserted without proof. It should follow from the local model, since a transversal intersection of a subfamily is transversal, but that requires the local identification with subspaces of Σ*(0) to be compatible across different points and charts.

ideas.what: Σ*(d) for a chain d is locally the transversal intersection of the boundary hypersurfaces Σ*({i_α, i_n}) ≅ Σ*(1) inside Σ*({i_n}) ≅ Σ*(0); that is, the unfolding is a manifold with (embedded) corners whose codimension-n faces are indexed by chains of length n+1.
ideas.modern_name: Resolution of a Thom-Mather stratified space into a manifold with corners with an iterated fibration structure (faces ↔ chains of strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goresky (thesis 1976, control data and blow-ups); Verona (abstract stratified spaces/resolutions, LNM 1102, 1984); Albin-Leichtnam-Mazzeo-Piazza (2012, 'resolution' to manifolds with corners); Ayala-Francis-Tanaka (unzipping, 2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 announces the 'déploiement' of stratified spaces into a system of manifolds with boundary indexed by flags, but without these axioms (to my knowledge)

ideas.what: Diagram (34): for cofinal d ⊂ d', the fan of intermediate chains d ∪ {j}, each bordant into Σ*(d), with Σ*(d') their transversal intersection.
ideas.modern_name: Boundary-face cube / 'multi-face' condition (Jänich's ⟨k⟩-manifolds: each face a union of faces, corners as transversal intersections)

ideas.what: Indexing the unfolded pieces by finite totally ordered sets with a functor contravariant in inclusions; cocartesian squares for pushouts of ordered sets; bordant vs fibrant maps according to whether the last element (resp. an initial segment) is preserved.
ideas.modern_name: Diagram of manifolds with corners over the poset of chains / subdivision (exit-path / 'link' category description of stratified spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ayala-Francis-Tanaka; Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A) for the ∞-categorical analogue; Mather/Thom control data classically

missed.claim: Grothendieck (1981-82) formulates an axiom system for the unfolding of a stratified space as a diagram of manifolds with boundary/corners indexed by chains. It includes the explicit condition that Σ*(d) be locally the transversal intersection of the bordant images of Σ*({i_α, i_n}), and its generalization (34) to all cofinal inclusions. This anticipates the 'resolution into manifolds with corners with iterated fibration structure' later made standard by Albin-Leichtnam-Mazzeo-Piazza and the unzipping of Ayala-Francis-Tanaka. The combinatorial packaging (functor on finite ordered sets, cocartesian conditions, bordant/fibrant dichotomy) is not in the literature under his name.
missed.quote: Σ*(d) soit l'intersection des Σ*_{i_α,i_n} (≃ Σ*(1)), et que cette famille soit transversale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an explicit, finitary, Δ-indexed axiomatization of conically smooth / Thom-Mather stratified spaces in terms of manifolds with corners. This is useful for comparing the AFT and ALMP approaches and the exit-path description, and it documents Grothendieck's unpublished realization of the Esquisse's 'déploiement' programme.

missed.claim: The compatibility between bordant maps (cofinal inclusions) and fibrant 'source' maps (initial-segment inclusions) is left open. So is the question whether the boundary structure of Σ*(d') is implied by the non-singularity condition (next page's marginal note).
missed.quote: on voit par là s'expliciter la condition de transversalité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is precisely the delicate point (iterated fibration structure: boundary fibrations commuting on corners) that later authors had to impose as an axiom.

deep.surprise_reason: The overall déploiement idea is announced in the Esquisse, and the corner/transversality structure is now standard (ALMP, AFT). The notable part is seeing Grothendieck in 1981-82 pin down the precise local corner axiom in a chain-indexed functorial form. That is a solid unpublished detail but not a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'dans Σ*_{\{i_α\}} ≃ Σ*(0)' should be 'dans Σ*({i_n}) ≃ Σ*(0)', the target of the maps in (33).
Line 2: 'Σ*_{\{α, i_α\}}' should be 'Σ*({i_α, i_n})', consistent with diagram (33) on the previous page.
'd, d' configurations (soit plongeant éléments)' is probably 'd, d' cofinaux (ont même plus grand élément)'.
'(ayant un élément supplémentaire sur d)' is probably '(cofinaux avec d)', i.e. same largest element.
In diagram (34) the intermediate terms are Σ*(d ∪ {j_1}) and Σ*(d ∪ {j_p}), with a dotted line between them; the transcription's 'd'∪j_1' is a slip for d ∪ {j_1}.
'tous morphismes d'[?]' is likely 'tous morphismes d'immersion' (cf. 'd'immersion' on p. 48).
'(génériquement : b)' likely refers back to condition (b).
